openingMessage: If you leave this meeting knowing one more thing than you walked in with, it worked. Let's make these ten minutes count.
openingWhy: The hand who fought a frozen pump hose trying to kill a well wrote it up on his OWL form — and now every crew that reads it learns that lesson the easy way. One form reaches every trailer in the Basin by morning. What you know only protects people if it moves.
leadershipThought: We win in this business by being invited back the next day. That doesn't just come from doing the job right — it comes from how we carry ourselves as professionals and as people.

concerns.title: Jordan Lemmons — XTO, Woodfin-Dollie W16C 3H, 09:45 AM, job 36441. Benzene detected above zero during the wellhead and flow line disconnect. The form records the reading
concerns.quote: Completed the job we did some some benzene of 0.71 so the mt requested to let it air out and rest so we didn't and got 0s so continued with job and got it finished

concerns.title: Cindy Smith (1099) — XTO, Woodfin-Dollie W16C 3H, 09:47 AM, job 36442. Same well and same operation as item 1, documented independently by the second technician
concerns.quote: Work area and bleeder valves tested prior to crew beginning work. Benzene was detected on first and second break but dissipated quickly. Crew was able to work without supplied air. Wellhead and flow line was disconnected. The job went according to plan with no incidents or near misses.

todaysChallenge: Yesterday's miss doesn't ride with you today — but its lesson does. Put the lesson on your OWL form where the whole crew can use it, then run today clean.
todaysChallengeSubtext: “What to do with a mistake: recognize it, admit it, learn from it, forget it.” — Dean Smith
